 Judgment
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of K.Suresh in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
2.

That, on 17.5.2024 at about 3.00 a.m, the deceased K.Suresh was riding his motor cycle bearing No.TN-23-DY-9387, on Chittoor to Palamaner NH-69 road, infront of Srini food factory, Bangarupalyam Mandal, at that time the driver of lorry, bearing registration No.JH-05-DK-2839 was parked unmindfully on the middle of the highway road without any indications like indicator lights, reflectors, manual signaling etc., the rider of the motor cycle inspite of careful riding of the motor cycle could not anticipate the unmindful parking of the lorry on the middle of the road dashed against the rear side of the lorry.
In the result, rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to Government Hospital, Chittoor, during the course of treatment the injured succumbed to the injuries.
3. It is further stated that, post mortem was conducted at District Hospital, Chittoor and the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony towards medicines and hospitalization of the deceased.

4. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
aged about 21 years, student.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have put to untold misery, pain, shock and mental agony.
5. It is further stated that, the accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of lorry, bearing registration No.JH-05-DK-2839.

6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court,
remained absent, hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, contended that petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.TN-23-DY- 9387 and not on the part of the lorry bearing No.JH- 05-DK-2839.
The IMV report clearly substantiate that there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
This respondent has admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of Lorry bearing No.JH-05-DK-2839 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that K.Suresh died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 17.5.2024 at about 3.00 a.m. on Chittoor to Palamaner NH-69 road, infront of Srini Food Factory, Bangarupalem Mandal,
Chittoor District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.JH-05-DK-2839 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
4) What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.

The petitioners examined one witness as PW2.
10.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its State Head as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.

R E A S O N S Issue No.1:
14.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.JH-05-DK-2839, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently K.Suresh had succumbed to the injuries.

15. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, he himself rode his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit the lorry.
The same is substantiated in the spot mahazar and spot sketch drawn by the jurisdictional police.
By considering the damages stated in the IMV report, it is clearly substantiated there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.

16. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
17. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.2 by name Hamsa, examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

sentences.text: On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement the father of the deceased K.Suresh, the SHO of Bangarupalem Police have registered the case against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable under Sections 304(A) of IPC.

Upon the investigation, the I.O. has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable u/s 304(A) of IPC.
19.
In support of the case of the petitioners, they have examined one eye witness as PW2.

He has deposed in his evidence that one lorry bearing No.JH- 05-DK-2839 was parked in the middle of the highway road without taking adequate due care and caution and without taking adequate due care and caution and without taking precautionary of putting sign boards, indicator lights, reflectors and manual signaling etc.
Inspite of careful riding, the rider of the motor cycle could not identify the unmindful parking of the lorry and dashed the motor cycle against the rear side of the lorry.
In the result rider fell down and sustained grievous head injuries and died during the course of treatment.
20. On the contrary, the respondent No.2 has examined its State Head as RW1.

He has deposed in his evidence that according to the IMV report, spot sketch and IMV analysis it is clearly substantiated that there is gross negligence on the part of the deceased rider of the Yamaha motor cycle bearing No.TN-23-DY-9387.

The alleged accident occurred was a National Highway i.e.,
NH-69, Chittoor- Palamaner Highway.

21. At the time of cross-examination of PW1 & PW2 though several questions put to them to show that, deceased was sole responsible for accident, nothing worthwhile is elicited from them to disprove the allegations made against the driver of the lorry.

22. Apart from this, the respondents herein, to disprove the point of contributory negligence in counter to the charge sheet, not made an effort to place evidence by producing the evidence of eye witnesses of the accident fully mentioned their names in the recitals of the charge sheet, as well as driver of the offending vehicle.

23. At the time of argument the counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied the following decision;
MFA No.689/1987 between Smt.Shakuntala & Others Vs. Loganathan & Others.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "even though stationary truck driver had not taken precautionary measures to indicate its parking, the deceased was also negligent in contributing to accident to an extent of 50%".

24. On the contrary, the counsel for the petitioner has relied the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in ACJ 2024 2161 between Sushma Vs. Nitin Ganapati Rangole & Others Wherein the Supreme Court of India held that, "on a holistic analysis of the material available on record, it is established beyond the pale of doubt that the offending truck was parked in the middle of the road without any parking any lights being switched on and without any markers or indicators been placed around the stationary vehicle, so as to warn the incoming vehicular trophy.

sentences.text: where the permissible speed limits are fairly high.

In such a situation, it would be imprudent to hold that the driver of a vehicle, travelling through the highway in the dead of the night in pitch dark conditions, would be able to make out a stationary vehicle lying in the middle of the road without a reasonable distance so as to apply the brakes and avoid the collusion.
The situation would be compounded by the head lights of the vehicle coming from the opposite direction and make the viewing of the stationary vehicle even more difficult.
Therefore driver of the incoming car cannot be held for negligence."

25. In the instant case also the driver of the lorry had stationed his vehicle without indicator without parking lights and the accident took place at about 3.00 a.m. on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69, the permissible speed limit are fairly high in the highway and in pitch dark condition it would be very difficult to make out the stationary vehicle lying in the road.
Hence, the decision relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner is aptly applicable to the facts of this case on hand.
26. Apart from this, it is not in dispute that, charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the lorry.
If the driver of the lorry would have taken more caution while parking his lorry, this accident would not have occurred.
27. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.
Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.JH-05-DK-2839 and in the said accident, K.Suresh succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 & 3:
28.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P8 to Ex.P12 Aadhar cards of the deceased and the petitioners and ration card, have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

29. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioner No.1 & 2 in their middle age, lost their son, as well as the care of their son, the petitioner No.3 has lost his brother, who was the backbone of the family.
The respondent herein has not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners.

30. The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased, as on the date of the accident,
have placed SSC Marks card marked at Ex.P14.
On going through said documents, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 6.9.2003.

sentences.text: The alleged accident had occurred on 17.5.2024.
Hence, I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 21 years.
For his age, multiplier '18' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

31. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition, and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, at the time of accident the deceased was doing his final year degree in Mother Theresa College, Palamaner.
If he would have completed his degree, he would have earned Rs.25,000/- per month.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioners have placed study and conduct certificate, SSC Marks card, intermediate marks card, ID card at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16.
On perusal of these, it is clear that the deceased was studyig degree.

Hence, it is apt to take the notional income, by looking into consideration of the year of accident along with other facts and circumstances of the case, as well as by looking in to the chart of the notional income of the Legal Services Authority.
Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m., for the year 2024, which will meet the ends of justice.

32. Another point to be taken in to consideration herein that, as per the petition, the deceased was a bachelor, for deduction of the personal and living expenses, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.
33. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
34.
Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.

In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor,
deduction towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 21 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "18" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the petitioner herein as on the date of the accident, was not having permanent job.

As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.

sentences.text: Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month. And Rs.1,98,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to (Rs.1,98,000+79,200)= Rs.2,77,200/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus net loss income comes to Rs.1,38,600/- (Rs.2,77,200- Rs.1,38,600).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "18".

Which comes to Rs.24,94,800/- .
35.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following decision;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others
, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz.,
loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/-
and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

36. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.18,150/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.18,150/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.48,400/- is awarded to the petitioner No.1 & 2 under the head loss of consortium.
37.

LIABILITY:-
39.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.JH-05-DK-2839, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
40. As per Ex.R2 the insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing No.JH-05-DK-2839 is valid from 30.3.2024 to 29.3.2025.
The alleged accident occurred on 17.5.2024.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Affirmative and the Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
41.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,27,900/- (Rupees twenty six lakhs twenty seven thousand and nine hundred only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 45% each and the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 10%.

 Judgment
opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of K.Suresh in a road traffic accident.
In the result, rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to Government Hospital, Chittoor, during the course of treatment the injured succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.TN-23-DY- 9387 and not on the part of the lorry bearing No.JH- 05-DK-2839.
The IMV report clearly substantiate that there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that K.Suresh died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 17.5.2024 at about 3.00 a.m. on Chittoor to Palamaner NH-69 road, infront of Srini Food Factory, Bangarupalem Mandal,
Chittoor District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.JH-05-DK-2839 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
4) What order or award?
16. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has assessed the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.30,000/- by relying the case of Radhakrishna Vs. Gokul 2013 (16) SCC 585, who was a student of Engineering course and expired in an accident.
By considering the damages stated in the IMV report, it is clearly substantiated there is gross negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
23. At the time of argument the counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied the following decision;
MFA No.689/1987 between Smt.Shakuntala & Others Vs. Loganathan & Others.
25. In the instant case also the driver of the lorry had stationed his vehicle without indicator without parking lights and the accident took place at about 3.00 a.m. on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69, the permissible speed limit are fairly high in the highway and in pitch dark condition it would be very difficult to make out the stationary vehicle lying in the road.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
2) 2024 ACJ 658 between Kumud Gupta & Another Vs. Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd., &
Others Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has confirmed the judgment and award passed in high court stating that, the High Court was justified in computing the monthly notional income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- per month and adding Rs.40% increased to the said income towards future prospects and since the deceased was not married by deducting 50% of the monthly income towards personal expenses".
13.
On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement the father of the deceased K.Suresh, the SHO of Bangarupalem Police have registered the case against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable under Sections 304(A) of IPC.
Upon the investigation, the I.O. has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable u/s 304(A) of IPC.
19.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
On perusal of these, it is clear that the deceased was studyig degree.
Hence, it is apt to take the notional income, by looking into consideration of the year of accident along with other facts and circumstances of the case, as well as by looking in to the chart of the notional income of the Legal Services Authority.
Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m., for the year 2024, which will meet the ends of justice.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
In the present case, deceased was aged about 21 years, as on the date of the accident.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the petitioner herein as on the date of the accident, was not having permanent job.
As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month. And Rs.1,98,000/- per year.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The alleged accident occurred on 17.5.2024.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to (Rs.1,98,000+79,200)= Rs.2,77,200/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.
Compensation heads Compensation  Amount
Towards loss of Rs.24,94,800-00  dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 96,800-00  consortium  Towards loss of estate Rs. 18,150-00  Towards funeral & Rs. 18,150-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses
Total Rs.26,27,900-00
Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.26,27,900/- (Rupees twenty six lakhs twenty seven thousand and nine hundred only), along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.
40. As per Ex.R2 the insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing No.JH-05-DK-2839 is valid from 30.3.2024 to 29.3.2025.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Affirmative and the Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.4:
41.
In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,27,900/- (Rupees twenty six lakhs twenty seven thousand and nine hundred only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 45% each and the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 10%.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 2, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.3, entire amount shall be released to him through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
